title: The Perfect Cipher
premise: Tamsin Zhou, a retired detective who traded homicide for a failing bookshop, is pulled back into investigation when a body appears dressed in clothes stolen from their own closet — a message meant for them alone. As Tamsin digs in, they discover the killer is someone from the case that ended their career twelve years ago: the one witness they protected, now grown and weaponizing everything Tamsin filed away. The murders reenact the old case file chapter by chapter, forcing Tamsin to choose between exposing their own buried complicity to stop the killer or protecting the person they once loved. In the end, Tamsin traps the killer using a deliberate error planted in the reconstructed file, but the cost is the truth coming out — and the town, and Tamsin's last chance at love, will never see them the same way again.
about_author: J. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing cold case files before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who know too much and say too little.

chapters.title: Alphabetical Order
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A quiet morning in the failing bookshop establishes Tamsin's meticulous routines, dwindling savings, and careful distance from the town that once needed them. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness — order as armor.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Police knock: a body found in the ravine wearing clothes stolen from Tamsin's own closet, down to the monogrammed scarf. Detective Priya Raghavan, once Tamsin's protégée, reluctantly asks for help. Beat: dread wrapped in flattery.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Filing
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Searching memory, Tamsin realizes the victim's pose mirrors the 2013 Marlow case — the file that ended their career. Flashback fragments surface: a young witness named Wren, a promise made. Beat: guilt stirring under dust.

chapters.title: Witness, Reluctant
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya interviews townsfolk while privately resenting needing her disgraced mentor. She notices the crime scene was staged with impossible precision — someone had access to sealed evidence photos. Beat: professional unease becoming suspicion.

chapters.title: The Borrower
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin discovers more items missing from the shop and apartment — a curated wardrobe being assembled elsewhere. A note left in a returned book reads only 'Chapter Two.' Beat: the hunter realizing they are also the quarry.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin tracks down Wren Calloway, now a respected grief counselor in the next county, and finds them calm, kind, and unnervingly fluent in details of the old case. Old tenderness flickers; so does fear. Beat: love against duty, first collision.

chapters.title: Chapter Three
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A second body, staged exactly like the file's third photograph. Priya conceals from her superiors how closely the scenes match restricted documents — because she signed out those documents herself, years ago, for Tamsin. Beat: complicity spreading.

chapters.title: What the File Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Reconstructing the 2013 case at the kitchen table, Tamsin confronts what they omitted from their official report: evidence they buried to protect Wren. Beat: the past demanding an audit of the self.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Caller
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A customer lingers over poetry, quoting lines Wren loved. Tamsin can't prove it was them. That night the shop window is shattered and every book on secrets is arranged face-out. Beat: intimacy weaponized.

chapters.title: Power Corrupts, Slowly
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's career advances on the case's publicity; she begins shaping the narrative rather than the truth, echoing the institutional rot that ruined Tamsin. Beat: the theme of corruption turning inward on our second lead.

chapters.title: Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin and Wren meet by the ravine. Wren nearly confesses, then pivots: 'You wrote me into a file. I'm just finishing your draft.' Tamsin leaves unsure whether they've been warned or seduced. Beat: longing braided with terror.

chapters.title: The Missing Chapter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Comparing murders to the file, Tamsin finds one scene unaccounted for — the night of the original crime no photograph ever captured. Whatever happened then exists only in two memories: Wren's and Tamsin's own suppressed one. Beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Power fails during a storm; Priya finds Tamsin sitting with the old file open, matches burning down. Each tests the other with half-truths. Neither names Wren. Beat: two keepers of secrets circling the same lock.

chapters.title: A Third Signature
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Forensics find traces of a third person at both scenes — someone who helped stage them. Priya suspects Tamsin; the department agrees. Tamsin is formally named a person of interest. Beat: the net closing on the wrong suspect, or the right one.

chapters.title: Everything I Kept for You
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin breaks into their own archived storage and finds the box of Wren's letters from 2013 — including one describing the original crime in detail that contradicts Tamsin's buried version. Beat: the foundation cracking; love revealed as cover story.

chapters.title: The Accomplice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (first time). We finally enter the killer's mind: wounded, brilliant, convinced they are completing Tamsin's true testimony. Their accomplice — the quiet bookshop regular — believes they're helping a survivor heal. Beat: chilling sympathy.

chapters.title: Chapter Twenty-Two
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The final murder is announced in advance: a note says the last scene will be 'the confession you never gave,' performed at the old courthouse. Tamsin understands the killer wants an audience of one. Beat: terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Raghavan's Choice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Ordered to arrest Tamsin before the courthouse event, Priya instead shows Tamsin the surveillance file — choosing truth over advancement, undoing her own corruption arc. Together they build a trap around the staged 'confession.' Beat: redemption through partnership.

chapters.title: The Perfect Cipher
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the courthouse, Tamsin delivers a false confession seeded with a deliberate factual error only the real reader of the original file would catch. Wren corrects it — publicly, fatally. Beat: the trap sprung with words instead of weapons.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Arrested, Wren tells Tamsin the whole of that missing night — and it damns them both less than Tamsin feared but shames them more than they admitted. 'You alphabetized me,' Wren says. 'I just wanted to be read.' Beat: grief without absolution.

chapters.title: Restocking
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin gives Priya the full buried evidence, accepts consequences, and reopens the shop — shelves reordered, secrets surrendered. Priya visits not as police but as a friend. Beat: quiet repair, earned at cost.

chapters.title: Uncatalogued
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. Months later, a postcard arrives with no return address: a single line from Wren, neither threat nor farewell. Tamsin files it under nothing at all, leaving it on the counter where customers can see. Beat: living with an unclosable case — love that outlasts duty's verdict.
